analysis: This unit is a test-only change: it adds the Swift test `readExactlyAssemblesShortReads` to provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/KVCacheSSD/SSDBlockStreamingTests.swift (head lines 259-283). It exercises `SSDBlockStore.readExactly(_:from:what:beforeRead:)` with a full read and with short reads. The test checks that the returned bytes are identical, that `startIndex == 0`, and that the per-read charge callbacks match expectations ([64, 0] and [64, 0, 0]). The test writes only to a UUID-named temporary fixture root and removes it afterward. It adds no production code, no changes to the DBK3 crypto, lookup-tag derivation, TTL, or storage-validation behavior, and no new attack surface. Relevant threat T-041 (SSD at-rest tier, DoS and read-bound accounting) is not weakened. The test would help catch regressions in bounded reads and read-charge accounting, which feed the onBytesRead budgeting that the existing cursor test also uses. Remaining integration question: the production change to `SSDBlockStore.readExactly` (short-read assembly, zero-charge retry semantics, and whether a loop on repeated zero-byte or short reads is bounded) is not in this unit. A reviewer of the source file should confirm that a malicious or slow external volume cannot make the loop spin indefinitely or bypass the read-byte bounds, and that authenticated-chunk size gates still run before allocation. Nothing in the supplied evidence shows a regression.
